newsitem.title: USA: Ohio school district faces rating review-Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Ohio school district faces rating review-Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service Inc plans to place the rating of an Ohio school district on review as a result of tax refunds it owes General Electric Company, said a rating agency analyst.

Bill Leech, a senior analyst at Moody's, said Lockland School District's A1 rating will be placed on review because the school district has projected it may owe a GE aircraft engine subsidiary $2.1 million in tax refunds.
Leech said the refund amount represents 33 percent of the school district's approximately $6 million general fund budget.
The Lockland school district, in suburban Cincinnati, is the only district that faces a rating review by Moody's, Leech said.

He said out of the 68 school districts affected by refunds of personal property taxes that various GE subsidiaries in Ohio overpaid, Moody's rates 17. He added that with the exception of Lockland schools, the there was no "really major credit impact" on the other rated districts.

The exact amount of refunds owed by the districts remains in question as GE has an appeal pending before the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals to resolve the refund amount established by the Ohio Department of Taxation. School districts have been basing the refunds they owe the company on refund notices sent out earlier this year to counties by the state taxation department.
The refund notices hit school districts the most because they, unlike Ohio cities and counties, rely heavily on property taxes.
